 When the music takes flight: Filipino ‘ARMYs’ cross borders to watch BTS live
 Pauline Joyce Pascual · 14 November 2026 · 11:59 PM PHT · 5 MIN READ 
 Filipino ARMYs travel overseas to see BTS perform, turning concert dates into opportunities for international adventures.
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save For some music fans, a concert means a night out. For BTS fans, particularly the group’s devoted ARMY, it can mean an international trip.
 From booking flights to Seoul and Singapore to securing accommodations in other Asian destinations, Filipino fans are increasingly turning concert attendance into an opportunity to travel. And when it comes to BTS, the distance does not necessarily matter. If the group is performing in another country, fans are willing to find their way there.
 This phenomenon, often called gig-tripping or concert tourism, reflects how fandom has evolved beyond streaming music, collecting merchandise and attending local fan gatherings. For many ARMYs, supporting BTS means experiencing their performances wherever the group takes the stage.
 Also read A playful world of collectibles shapes Bangkok 
 The dedication is hardly exclusive to Filipino fans, but the Philippines has become an important market in the growing movement of music-driven travel.
 A growing travel trend among Filipino fans 
 The numbers help explain why this kind of travel is gaining momentum.
 According to Visa’s 2024 Green Shoots Radar study, Filipino concertgoers ranked among the top five in Asia-Pacific for overseas concert travel. Among Filipino respondents who traveled abroad for music concerts, 37 percent said they planned their trips specifically around these events. South Korea and Singapore emerged as two of their preferred destinations.
 BTS has been a major part of this movement.
 Also read Galilea’s sea of possibilities 
 In February 2026, a 17-percent increase in visa applications from Filipinos in January and February, as many prepared to travel to South Korea for the group’s comeback concert. South Korean Ambassador Lee Sang-hwa said the embassy expected the number of Filipino visitors during the first two months of the year to increase from the usual 13,000 to approximately 20,000. The embassy traced the increase partly to the anticipation surrounding BTS’ March 21 performance in Seoul.
 The enthusiasm also extends beyond the group’s full lineup. In 2023, Filipino musicians and longtime ARMYs traveled to Bangkok and Singapore to catch SUGA’s Agust D solo tour.
 Among them were Myrene, bassist of Sandwich and Imago, and Maysh, vocalist of Moonstar88. Myrene initially planned to attend the Bangkok show but eventually booked another flight to Singapore after friends persuaded her to catch a second performance.
 Maysh, meanwhile, watched three shows across Bangkok and Singapore. She described how she and fellow ARMYs coordinated their ticketing strategies, planned which concert dates to pursue and helped one another secure seats.
 Their experiences, documented by music publication Bandwagon, show how fandom can become a shared travel experience, with friends coordinating flights, concert tickets and itineraries around their favorite artist.

 More than the concert itself 
 For many fans, the appeal of flying abroad goes beyond seeing their idols perform.
 A concert trip can also mean exploring a new city, discovering local food, visiting tourist attractions and meeting fellow fans from different parts of the world. The concert becomes the centerpiece of a much bigger holiday.
 A November 2026 report, citing Klook’s Travel Pulse 2026, found that 90 percent of Filipino travelers who went abroad for concerts extended their stays to explore their destinations. Of these travelers, 78 percent stayed for up to four additional days.
 The findings suggest that concert tourism is creating opportunities for travelers to combine entertainment with cultural experiences and sightseeing.
 The economic impact can also be significant. Visa’s analysis found that Filipino concertgoers who traveled overseas spent 58 percent more during their trips than non-concertgoers. Shopping was their leading expenditure, followed by purchases involving apparel, accessories and retail experiences.
 South Korea has likewise seen the tourism benefits of BTS-related travel. According to an analysis by the country’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, international visitors who attended the group’s March 2026 Gwanghwamun comeback performance stayed an average of 8.7 days and spent approximately 3.53 million won per person. This was longer and higher than the averages recorded for general international visitors during the first quarter of the year.
 The price of following your favorite group 
 Of course, traveling for a concert requires more than enthusiasm. Fans have to consider airfare, accommodation, concert tickets, transportation, meals and merchandise. For international shows, these expenses can quickly add up, particularly when tickets sell out and hotel rates rise around concert dates.
 In a March 2026 feature, CNA Lifestyle spoke with ARMYs planning to follow BTS across several stops of its ARIRANG world tour. Some had already secured tickets for concerts in Europe and Asia, while others were preparing to book additional destinations.
 CONCERT tourism brings fans together across borders, with BTS among the artists
inspiring international travel.
 CONNIE FRANCE
 The fans also shared practical ways to manage expenses, including redeeming airline miles, booking accommodations with free cancellation, sharing hotel rooms with fellow fans and setting a spending limit before traveling.
 One fan also advised fellow ARMYs to assess their finances before committing to multiple concert dates, emphasizing that loving BTS does not mean having to spend beyond one’s means.
 For Filipino fans, the excitement is particularly meaningful as BTS is also scheduled to perform in the Philippines on March 13 and 14, 2027, giving local ARMYs an opportunity to see the group on home ground. Still, the prospect of catching additional shows overseas remains part of the appeal for those who want to experience different concert venues and connect with international fan communities.
 Ultimately, flying abroad for BTS is not simply about crossing borders for a few hours of music. It is about the anticipation of seeing the group live, the friendships formed along the way and the memories created in a city that becomes temporarily connected by a shared love for seven artists.
 For ARMYs, a passport stamp can carry a special meaning. Sometimes, the destination is not just Seoul, Singapore or Bangkok. It is wherever BTS is taking the stage.
